question: Think of a career decision you have made or are weighing now. What are the two or three considerations that actually decide it for you, and which one wins when they conflict?
Describe a belief or decision of yours that you changed in the last year. What did you believe before, what new fact or experience changed it, and what principle do you use now?
When you face a choice between building something yourself and using an existing tool or service, how do you decide? Walk through a real example and say what tipped it.
How do you decide that a problem you are working on is not worth more of your time? Give a concrete case where you stopped, or where you wish you had.
When someone you respect gives you advice that you disagree with, what do you do with it? Describe a real instance and how you resolved it.
How much risk are you willing to take with money, time or reputation for something you believe in, and what is the line you will not cross?
How do you actually learn a hard technical subject so that it stays with you? Describe what you do in the first week, and what you do when you are stuck.
When two things you care about compete for the same evening, how do you choose between them? Use a recent real conflict and say what you gave up.
What makes you trust a tool or a person's work enough to rely on it, and what makes you stop trusting it? Give an example of each.
How do you know when your own work is finished? Describe the last thing you called done and what you checked before saying so.
Describe a trade-off between speed and quality that you handled recently. What did you choose, why, and would you choose the same again?
Pick a mistake that cost you something real. What was your reasoning at the time, where did it go wrong, and what do you do differently now?
When the honest answer to a question is something the other person will not want to hear, how do you handle it? Give an example from your own life.
What principles do you use for spending or saving money when it is tight? Describe one purchase decision you thought hard about and how you settled it.
What does your best working day look like and what reliably ruins it? Describe the conditions you set up deliberately.
How far ahead do you plan your work and your life, and what do you refuse to plan? Explain the reasoning behind where you draw that line.
What early signs tell you that a project of yours is going to fail, and how soon do you act on them? Describe an example.
How do you want someone to disagree with you, and how do you disagree with others? Describe an exchange where this went well or badly.
What are you trying to build or become over the next few years, and what would make you change that goal? Be specific about what would count as evidence.
How do you decide when to rest and when to push through? Describe a recent time you made that call and how it turned out.
When you explain something to someone who is new to it, what do you do differently from when you explain it to an expert, and why? Give an example.
What do you believe makes a system you build durable, as opposed to merely working today? Illustrate with something you built or fixed.
Which of your own habits or opinions would you least like to see written down about you, and why? What does that tell you about what you value?
What do you do when you do not know something and nobody around you does either? Describe the last time that happened and what you did.
If you could only keep three of your current projects or commitments for the next year, which would you keep and what would you drop? Explain how you decided.
